report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of 25 (lines 241-342) of daedalus/spine/picker.py: Candidate and PickedQueue dataclasses.
risks: Candidate.to_dict | medium | score and band are floats; rounding may cause precision issues in serialization. | Check if rounding is acceptable or if decimal is needed.

Candidate.correctness_before_state | medium | Comment says 'carried, never re-derived here', but the field is a Mapping; no validation that it contains 'verified' key. | Add validation or clarify contract.
PickedQueue.sources | low | Typed as Mapping[str, Any] but used as dict; frozen dataclass may cause mutation issues. | Ensure usage is read-only or use dict type.

claims.text: evidence is the audit trail: it names the file the numbers came from and carries the numbers themselves, so a human reading the review packet can re-derive the score without re-running the picker.
claims.why: The claim describes intended use, but the code does not enforce or verify this structure. No validation of evidence contents is present.

claims.text: score and band are floats; rounding may cause precision issues in serialization.
claims.why: offset uses round(score - band, 4). This claim is a risk observation, not a code claim. But as a claim about behavior: it is kept because rounding occurs.

claims.text: carried, never re-derived here, because ranking a queue must not run pytest.
claims.why: The comment states that correctness_before_state is carried and not re-derived. The code does not re-derive it; it simply stores the value. However, the claim about 'must not run pytest' is about external behavior not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: Imported lazily: ranking a queue must not drag in the ledger, the worktree manager and the storage watermark, so --dry-run stays a read of two JSON files.
claims.why: The lazy import is visible (from daedalus.spine.attempt import TaskSpec inside the method). The claim about --dry-run and reading two JSON files is external and cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: A picker that prints nothing when a file is missing teaches the operator that there is no work; this one says which file it could not read.
claims.why: The docstring describes behavior of the picker (not in this chunk) and that PickedQueue provides informative output. The claim about printing file names is not verifiable from this code.

observations.what: Candidate.to_task_spec imports lazily, but the import is inside the method.
PickedQueue.degraded_sources property is incomplete; no implementation shown.
Candidate.to_dict includes a key 'before_state_verified' as bool, but correctness_before_state is a Mapping; it checks for 'verified' key.
